title: Kroger Cuts 3,000 Jobs to Trim Corporate Workforce
summary:
The grocery giant is restructuring its organizational hierarchy to increase productivity and speed up business decisions. CEO Greg Foran notified staff in a memo that the company will cut more than 1/3 of its corporate headcount, totaling roughly 3,000 roles, over the next 3 years to make the business leaner and more competitive. Kroger also plans to increasingly adopt artificial intelligence to streamline operations and reduce the need for back-office staff.

The layoffs follow the establishment of a "Global Capability Center" in India, which consultant Brittain Ladd reported aims for $500M in annual labor savings. Foran, who led Walmart US from 2014 to 2019, has also replaced several top executives with former Walmart colleagues, including Chief Store Operations Officer Mark Ibbotson and Chief E-commerce Officer Nate Faust.

selectedTweets.text:
KROGER SLASHING 3,000 MORE AMERICANS TODAY AS THEY OUTSOURCE JOBS TO INDIA

Greg Foran became Kroger CEO on February 9, 2026. He ran Walmart US from 2014 to 2019. In 2016 he pulled accounting and invoicing out of every store and erased 7,000 back office jobs. 

In 2018 Walmart handed its finance and accounting operations to Genpact, a firm with most of its workforce in India.

NOW HE IS USING THE SAME PLAYBOOK TO CUT JOBS AT KROGER

On his first earnings call in March, Kroger announced the Indian “Global Capability Center." CFO David Kennerley told investors it would "streamline decision-making, improve productivity and increase the speed at which we execute."

In July, consultant Brittain Ladd, citing people inside Kroger, reported the center is in India and the target is $500M a year in labor savings. At $87,500 per offshored role, that is roughly 5,700 US jobs.

3,000 MORE OF THEM CAME TODAY

His memo to employees today: “Our business is becoming leaner, more focused and more competitive. This transformation will also result in fewer roles across the company, which means we will reduce our corporate workforce across many functions.”

Code for, fuck your job, I can get it done cheaper in India.

Just look at what Foran has done with his executives. Jamie Lancaster, Global VP of the Kroger Capability Center, out in May. Tim Massa, Chief Associate Experience Officer, out. Valerie Jabbar and Joe Kelley, SVPs of Retail Divisions, out.

Foran replaced them with Walmart people. Mark Ibbotson is now Chief Store Operations Officer. Nate Faust is Chief E-commerce Officer. Both worked at Walmart with Foran. 

Both know how to help Foran outsource American jobs.
